event: Sunlight focused by a lens into a water jet is totally internally reflected at each incidence and follows the jet's bends as in a canal.

notes: Comptes rendus vol. 15 (1842), journal pp.800-802 = text.md pp.1-3. No session or publication date is printed on these pages, so date is empty (year 1842 from papers.csv). Scan with OCR (fr-FR); wording checked on page renders made from source.pdf in a scratchpad (figures/ holds no page_NN.png renders: img_pNN_1 / img_pNN_2 are scan layer separations, blank background and an unreadable mask). The letter has no figure, so key figure fields are empty. Byline prints only 'M. Colladon'; no affiliation is printed. No 'first' claim; priority paragraph (p.2-3): the experiments predate by several months Plateau's note read at the Brussels Academy on 1842-07-04; the Conservatoire des Arts et Metiers in Paris has held one of his devices, built by M. Bourbouze at M. Pouillet's request, since October 1841; copies were made for public courses in London; all results were repeated in the Geneva physics and mechanics courses in June 1841. Apparatus (p.1): vessel 1 m high, horizontal jet from screw-in diaphragms, convex lens in the opposite wall, blackened tube, sunlight sent by a mirror into a darkened room. Light escapes where the jet meets a solid or breaks into drops (p.2). p.1 top carries the end of a preceding zoology note; p.3 carries Babinet's follow-up note (candle-lit water stream, bent glass rods) and an organic chemistry note, not part of this letter.
